clue.text: One glorious retreat between five and six on islands — it implies I gave the enemy no chance!

definitions.text: it implies I gave the enemy no chance!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the earlier pieces
between places the reversed word and the single letter inside the pair of Roman numerals

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word for glorious is read in reverse

parts.note: glorious can mean divine, heavenly
I is the Roman numeral for one
CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A tale of one heroic withdrawal, timed between five and six o'clock, on some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reads the word for glorious backwards, 'between' sets that and One inside five and six, and 'on' puts the islands below in a down clue; 'retreat' misleads, as Caesar's phrase is a boast of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar's boast 'I came, I saw, I conquered' claims a victory so swift the enemy never had a chance.

clue.text: Ringing of bells around Ireland gets one in an erogenous zone

indicators.note: around says the ringing word wraps about the name for Ireland

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of bells ringing in Ireland putting someone in the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The perineum, between the genitals and anus, is an erogenous area, and this adjective describes things located there.

clue.text: Gunfire has journalist heading off repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the shortened word appears twice in a row
heading off says the first letter of the journalist word is dropped

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a jobbing one

explanation.surface: A reporter keeps setting off, under fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ack-ack is old military slang for anti-aircraft fire, from the signallers' spelling of AA.

clue.text: Audibly show contempt for an offence — one's more than a heel!

indicators.note: audibly says the phrase is to be heard, not read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: show contempt for is mock, and an offence is a sin, giving mock a sin

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at wrongdoing, and the heel in question is a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' seems to mean a scoundrel; here it is part of a shoe, and the whole soft shoe is more than just its heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather shoe, so it is footwear consisting of much more than its heel.

clue.text: Popular panel may be wounding

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a jury is a panel deciding a verdict

explanation.surface: A popular jury may deliver a hurtful verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurting someone, the act of wounding, is harm or damage, the noun sense of the definition.

clue.text: See 22
Dramatist can't reintegrate plays

indicators.note: plays means moves about freely, so the letters are rearranged; also a nod to the playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright who is unable to put his plays back together again.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English playwright, author of The Winslow Boy and The Browning Version.

clue.text: Doctor at filming location when a certain body sinks

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
on set means at the place where filming happens

explanation.surface: A medic on a film shoot at the moment someone collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain body' sounds like a person; it is the heavenly body seen at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon is a celestial body, and its setting below the horizon is the moment it sinks out of view.

clue.text: See 1
Opposing the monarch's entourage in battle

parts.note: agin is a dialect word for against, opposing
a court is the retinue around a king or queen

explanation.surface: Resistance to a king and his followers, fought out in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle in which Henry V's English army defeated the French.

clue.text: Measure of opposition that is restricting politician on trip

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the first part
restricting means holding in, so the abbreviation for that is encloses the politician

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
MP is a Member of Parliament
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Political opposition holding back an MP on a foreign trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposition' suggests politics; here it is electrical opposition to current.
explanation.definitionFit: In electronics, this quantity measures how strongly a circuit resists alternating current.

clue.text: Deviate from strict formation thus to find snark?

parts.note: rearranging the letters of ... gives snark, so splitting them up, an instruction to ... them, finds it

explanation.surface: A quest for Lewis Carroll's mythical Snark, achieved by abandoning discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer says to shuffle the word RANKS, which yields SNARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who step out of their lines leave the formation; figuratively, anyone departing from a united group.

clue.text: Yesteryear's maestro's lost in the morning in the wood

indicators.note: lost says that the morning abbreviation is removed from the conductor's name

parts.note: Sir Thomas Beecham was a famous British conductor of the past
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: An old conductor wanders lost one morning among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is a hardwood tree and its timber, so it names a kind of wood.

clue.text: Use piety falsely as a High Church type

indicators.note: falsely means wrongly, so the letters are set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A churchman accused of a hypocritical show of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Edward Pusey, a leader of the Oxford Movement, were Anglo-Catholics, High Churchmen.

clue.text: Lies in legal writ

definitions.meaning: stories, as in telling stories, means untruths
in law, a writ summoning extra jurors when the panel is short

explanation.surface: Falsehoods tucked into a court document.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall stories are fibs, and a tales is an old writ calling bystanders to fill a jury.

clue.text: See 21 down
One had one's work cut out getting man to embrace woman

definitions.text: One had one's work cut out

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold around, so the man's name goes round the woman's

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
Di is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man hugging a woman, and someone with a demanding job ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had one's work cut out' sounds like facing a hard task; literally, a sculptor cuts out his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor, carving and modelling works like The Thinker.

clue.text: See 7
See 21 down
Mechanical device to give girl breathing difficulties

parts.note: to be short of wind is to have trouble breathing
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A machine built to leave a young woman gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch, a drum turned by a crank for hauling rope or chain.

clue.text: Wilder fashion — something that gets under the skin, initially?

indicators.note: initially says the skin-piercing item comes first, before the fashion word

parts.words: something that gets under the skin
parts.note: a thorn can lodge beneath the skin
ton is fashion, the fashionable world

explanation.surface: A wilder trend: something irritating that works its way under the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like a comparative adjective; it is the American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thornton Wilder was the American playwright of Our Town, so his first name identifies him.

clue.text: Unruly behaviour brings strain to port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port, often just Rio
to try is to strain or exert oneself

explanation.surface: Rowdy conduct puts pressure on a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotry is a rare word for rioting, disorderly or riotous conduct.

clue.text: See 12
Change needed for Easter — put in new pews?

indicators.note: change says the letters of the festival's name must be altered

explanation.surface: A church needs alterations for the Easter congregation, perhaps new seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting a church with fresh seats is giving it new seating, and pews are church benches.

clue.text: Deceitful types watch grandfather, maybe

definitions.meaning: people who cheat on partners, being unfaithful
a watch and a grandfather clock are a pair of timepieces

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on grandpa: he might be a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like a verb; it is a wristwatch, and grandfather is the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfaithful by courting two lovers is cheating; and a pair of clocks is literally a couple of timepieces.

clue.text: The enemy archer we can't expect to know immediately

definitions.text: we can't expect to know immediately

parts.note: time is often called the enemy, as in time is the enemy
William ... was the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A hostile bowman whose secrets we will not learn at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the truth will emerge only eventually, so answers cannot be had at once.

clue.text: Southeast European first to last has little 21 down or place for romance

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter of the nationality is moved to the end

parts.note: a Slovene is a person from Slovenia
the first word of 21 down is abbreviated to the letter t

explanation.surface: A Balkan visitor with a brief moment to spare looks for somewhere romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves S to the end, making LOVENES.
explanation.definitionFit: A love nest is a cosy hideaway where lovers meet, a spot for courtship.

clue.text: See 1
Italian in the Lake District, maybe, when it's less cold

indicators.note: less means without, so the cold abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: Cumbrian describes Cumbria, the county containing England's Lake District
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Italian holidaying in the English Lakes when the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous area of northwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a region of central Italy, so a native of it is Italian.

clue.text: Fool wearing something with feathers as long garment

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the feathered bird goes around the fool

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, covered in feathers
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown in a feathered costume dressed in a lengthy robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is the full-length robe worn by clergy and choristers.
